quiz.question: On July 23, 2026, India observed National Broadcasting Day to commemorate the first organized radio broadcast in the country. Which anniversary of India's first organized radio broadcast did the year 2026 mark?
quiz.explanation: National Broadcasting Day is celebrated on July 23 every year to mark the first organized radio broadcast in India, which was carried out by the Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) from the Bombay station in 1927. The year 2026 marks the 99th anniversary of this historic event. The IBC was a private entity that was eventually taken over by the Government of India, leading to the creation of the Indian State Broadcasting Service in 1930 and All India Radio (AIR) in 1936.

quiz.question: Which of the following organizations prepared 'AAROH', India's first comprehensive annual report on scientific mine closure and repurposing, released in July 2026?
quiz.explanation: The Union Ministry of Coal released 'AAROH: Annual Report on Mine Closure', which is India's first comprehensive documentation of scientific mine closure and repurposing practices. Prepared by the Coal Controller Organisation (CCO), the report highlights the reclamation processes of 42 scientifically closed coal mines. During the launch event, the government also signed an agreement with Germany's GIZ to implement advanced technical practices for mine restoration and sustainable post-mining land use.

quiz.question: In July 2026, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) signed contracts with industry partners to convert which of the following commercial aircraft models into the green configuration for the Airborne Early Warning and Control (AEW&C) Mk-II Programme?
quiz.explanation: The DRDO's Centre for Air Borne Systems (CABS) signed major contracts with AI Engineering Services Limited (AIESL) and Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited (ADSTL) for the AEW&C Mk-II Programme. Under these contracts, six commercial Airbus A321 aircraft acquired from Air India will be converted into green configurations to serve as the platform for mounting indigenous airborne mission systems. Approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security with an outlay of Rs. 19,000 crore, the first induction is planned for 2032-2033.

quiz.question: According to the factsheet on cotton released by the Government of India in July 2026, what is India's global rank in terms of cotton cultivation area and cotton production respectively?
options: First in cultivation area, First in production
First in cultivation area, Second in production
Second in cultivation area, First in production
Second in cultivation area, Second in production
quiz.explanation: A comprehensive factsheet released by the Government of India in July 2026 highlights cotton as India's 'White Gold', which supports 6 million farmers and around 40-50 million people across the textile chain. Globally, India ranks first in cotton cultivation area, covering 114.84 lakh hectares (about 38% of the global cotton area). Additionally, India ranks second globally in both cotton production and consumption, contributing approximately 19% of the world's total fibre production.

quiz.question: To commemorate the birth anniversary of the great freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak on July 23, several national tributes were paid. In which year did he co-found the Deccan Education Society in Pune to foster nationalistic education?
quiz.explanation: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, born on July 23, 1856, in Ratnagiri, Maharashtra, was a pioneer of the Extremist phase of the Indian national movement. In 1884, he co-founded the Deccan Education Society in Pune alongside Gopal Ganesh Agarkar and others to provide high-quality, nationalistic education to the masses, which eventually led to the establishment of Fergusson College. He also popularized public celebrations of Ganesh Utsav (1893) and Shivaji Jayanti (1895) to instill national pride.

quiz.question: In July 2026, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote green, climate-resilient, and sustainable infrastructure projects with MAHAPREIT. MAHAPREIT is a state enterprise of which of the following state governments?
quiz.explanation: NABARD signed an MoU with Mahatma Phule Renewable Energy and Infrastructure Technology Limited (MAHAPREIT), an enterprise of the Government of Maharashtra. This partnership aims to jointly finance and implement green, climate-resilient, and sustainable projects such as the decarbonization of government buildings, Gram Panchayat infrastructure, solar-powered agricultural pumping, and bioenergy/biogas plants in rural India, with an initial geographic focus on Maharashtra.

quiz.question: During the official visit of Zanzibar President Hussein Ali Mwinyi to India in July 2026, the master plan for the 200-acre international campus of which Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) was unveiled at Fumba Peninsula, Zanzibar?
quiz.explanation: Zanzibar President Hussein Ali Mwinyi paid an official visit to India from July 17 to 20, 2026. During this visit, he attended the 63rd Convocation of IIT Madras and unveiled the comprehensive master plan for the 200-acre IIT Madras Zanzibar campus at Fumba Peninsula. This campus represents India's first international IIT campus and is designated as a Centre of Excellence for higher education and technology in the African continent.

quiz.question: During President Droupadi Murmu's state visit to Romania in July 2026, the first visit by an Indian head of state in over three decades, the two countries signed three agreements. At which university will a Chair of Indian Studies be established under the education agreement?
quiz.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu visited Bucharest, Romania in July 2026, marking the first visit by an Indian head of state to the country in more than 30 years. Following bilateral delegation-level talks, India and Romania signed three landmark agreements covering Science and Technology, Sports, and Indian Studies. Under the education and Indian studies MoU, a dedicated Chair of Indian Studies will be established at the University of Bucharest with support from the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).

quiz.question: The Karlapat Bauxite Block, which was in the news in July 2026 due to the interest shown by several major Indian mining companies, is a greenfield mining block located in which state?
quiz.explanation: The Karlapat Bauxite Block is a major greenfield mining block located in the Kalahandi district of Odisha. It came into focus in July 2026 as prominent Indian corporations, including Adani, Reliance Industries, Hindalco, Vedanta Aluminium, and Coal India, expressed strong interest in its bidding. The block contains high-grade bauxite with approximately 45.2% alumina content. Odisha is a critical region for aluminum production, accounting for about 41% of India's total bauxite resources.

quiz.question: In July 2026, researchers from the Agharkar Research Institute (ARI) discovered five new species of Allographa lichen-forming fungi in the Western Ghats. In which city of Maharashtra is this autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) located?
quiz.explanation: Researchers from the Agharkar Research Institute (ARI) in Pune, Maharashtra, discovered five new species of Allographa lichen-forming fungi in the Western Ghats of Kerala. The newly identified species include Allographa keralensis and Allographa nayakae (named after Indian lichenologist Dr. Sanjeeva Nayaka). ARI Pune is a prestigious autonomous institute operating under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.
